## Walkthrough

This pull request updates the npm publish GitHub Actions workflow file. The changes include: adding a new branch condition (`ms-fix-npm-publish`) to trigger workflows on push events, introducing GitHub Actions permissions for `id-token` (write) and `contents` (read), upgrading the Node.js matrix version from 22.x to 24.x, updating `actions/checkout` from v4 to v6, updating `actions/setup-node` from v4 to v6, and modifying the publish step to perform a dry run instead of actual publishing while removing NODE_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable usage.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 2 (Simple) | ⏱️ ~8 minutes

### npm package provenance (GitHub Actions) — requirements

**To publish with provenance using `npm publish --provenance`:**
- **npm CLI ≥ 9.5.0** (older npm doesn’t support provenance). [1]
- Publish from a **supported cloud CI/CD** on a **cloud-hosted runner** (GitHub Actions on **GitHub-hosted** runners, e.g. `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`). [1]
- Workflow must be able to mint an OIDC token:  
  `permissions: { id-token: write }` [1]
- `package.json` must include a **public `repository` URL that matches (case-sensitive) the repo you’re publishing from**. [1]
- Use `npm publish --provenance` (and for a **first-time publish**, also set `--access public`). [1]

**If you use “Trusted Publishing” (OIDC) instead of an npm token:**
- **npm CLI ≥ 11.5.1**. [2]
- Only supported from **GitHub Actions (GitHub-hosted runners)** (self-hosted runners not supported as of now). [2]
- Workflow still needs `permissions: { id-token: write }`. [2]
- You must **configure the package’s Trusted Publisher** on npm to point at the exact GitHub repo + workflow (fields are exact / case-sensitive). [2]
- **Provenance is generated automatically** when publishing via trusted publishing (you typically **don’t need** `--provenance`), but provenance generation is limited to **public repos + public packages** (not supported for private source repos). [2]

**References:** npm provenance docs [1], npm trusted publishers (OIDC) docs [2].

---
